I found no bugs in the uncommitted change. It is one new untracked file, `orders/status.py`.

- **`latest_status` (line 13):** `order.events[-1]` can't raise `IndexError`. `Order.__post_init__` in `orders/model.py` always appends a `created` event, and events are never removed.
- **`notify_status` (lines 16–22):** It logs the failure and re-raises, so the caller still sees the error. The only side effect is that a caller who also logs the exception will log it twice. That is a style point, not a bug.

There is one latent issue outside the diff, in `orders/model.py:21-22`. If anyone builds `Order(id, events=[...])` with existing events, for example when rehydrating from storage, `__post_init__` appends a fresh `created` event at the end. `latest_status` would then report `created` for an order that has really progressed. Nothing in the repo does this today, so it only matters if you add a loader.

I only read the files. I didn't run any code, and the repo has no tests.
